proposals.before: Ran Min's governor of Zhangwu, Jia Jian, led county militia against Murong Ping at Gaocheng; Ping captured Jia Jian on the field and took more than three thousand heads.
proposals.after: Ran Min's governor of Zhangwu, Jia Jian, led commandery troops against Murong Ping at Gaocheng; Ping captured Jia Jian on the field and took more than three thousand heads.
proposals.reason: 郡兵 are commandery troops; Zhangwu is a commandery (章武太守), not a county, so "county militia" mistranslates the unit.

proposals.before: The Han honored Xiao He and Cao Cao above the peerage, granting them the right to wear sword and shoes in the audience hall and to enter court without the quickened step.
proposals.after: The Han honored Xiao He and Cao Shen above the peerage, granting them the right to wear sword and shoes in the audience hall and to enter court without the quickened step.
proposals.reason: 蕭、曹 paired as the Han founding chancellors are Xiao He and Cao Shen (曹參), whose court privileges are cited; Cao Cao lived centuries later.

proposals.before: Duan Kan's governor of Xuzhou, Wang Teng, and the Wuhuan chanyu Xue Yun went over to Murong Ke.
proposals.after: Duan Kan's governor of Xuzhou, Wang Teng, and the Suotou chanyu Xue Yun went over to Murong Ke.
proposals.reason: 索頭 (Suotou, "braided heads") designates the Tuoba Xianbei, not the Wuhuan.

proposals.before: Forty-nine years later it still ran like new; Murong Jun likened it to Bao Shuya's famous team, ordered a bronze statue cast in its image, inscribed his own eulogy on the flank, and set it up outside the east portal of Ji.
proposals.after: By now it was forty-nine years old yet still swift; Murong Jun likened it to the Bao family's dappled steed, ordered a bronze statue cast in its image, inscribed his own eulogy on the flank, and set it up outside the east portal of Ji.
proposals.reason: 至是，四十九歲矣 states the horse's age, not an interval; 鮑氏驄 is "the Bao family's dappled horse," not Bao Shuya's team.

proposals.before: Meanwhile Feng Yuan of Shangdang declared himself governor and leaned on Zhang Ping; Ping interceded repeatedly, and Murong Jun, for Ping's sake, forgave him and named him governor of Jingzhao.
proposals.after: Meanwhile Feng Yang of Shangdang declared himself governor and leaned on Zhang Ping; Ping interceded repeatedly, and Murong Jun, for Ping's sake, forgave him and named him governor of Jingzhao.
proposals.reason: 馮鴦 is read Feng Yang (鴦 yāng); "Feng Yuan" misromanizes the name.

proposals.before: Lü Hu and Feng Yuan were also in secret contact with the Jin court.
proposals.after: Lü Hu and Feng Yang were also in secret contact with the Jin court.
proposals.reason: 馮鴦 is read Feng Yang (鴦 yāng); "Feng Yuan" misromanizes the name.

proposals.before: Murong Jun sent his minister Murong Ping against Zhang Ping, his marshal Moyu Gen against Feng Yuan, his minister of works Yang Wu against Gao Chang, and his general Murong Zang against Li Li.
proposals.after: Murong Jun sent his minister Murong Ping against Zhang Ping, his marshal Moyu Gen against Feng Yang, his minister of works Yang Wu against Gao Chang, and his general Murong Zang against Li Li.
proposals.reason: 馮鴦 is read Feng Yang (鴦 yāng); "Feng Yuan" misromanizes the name.

proposals.before: Zhang Ping then bolted to Pingyang with three thousand men; Feng Yuan, Li Li, and Gao Chang scattered to Yewang, Xingyang, and Shaoling, each yielding his troops.
proposals.after: Zhang Ping then bolted to Pingyang with three thousand men; Feng Yang, Li Li, and Gao Chang scattered to Yewang, Xingyang, and Shaoling, each yielding his troops.
proposals.reason: 馮鴦 is read Feng Yang (鴦 yāng); "Feng Yuan" misromanizes the name.

proposals.before: Only after Shi Hu's host collapsed did he present himself to the Yan army and yield.
proposals.after: Only after his own troops collapsed did he present himself to the Yan army and yield.
proposals.reason: 眾潰 refers to Li Chan's own forces collapsing; Shi Hu is not named in this sentence.

proposals.before: Kan's appointed inspector of Xuzhou Wang Teng and Wuhuan shanyu Xue Yun surrendered to Ke.
proposals.after: Kan's appointed inspector of Xuzhou Wang Teng and Suotou (Tuoba) shanyu Xue Yun surrendered to Ke.
proposals.reason: 索頭 designates the Tuoba Xianbei (“braided heads”), not the Wuhuan; the idiomatic repair already proposes this, and the sealed literal still says Wuhuan.

proposals.before: Moreover Shangdang Feng Yuan styled himself governor, attached to Zhang Ping; Ping repeatedly spoke of him; Jun because of Ping's sake, pardoned his crime, appointed him Jingzhao governor.
proposals.after: Moreover Shangdang Feng Yang styled himself governor, attached to Zhang Ping; Ping repeatedly spoke of him; Jun because of Ping's sake, pardoned his crime, appointed him Jingzhao governor.
proposals.reason: 馮鴦 is Feng Yang (鴦 yāng); the sealed literal still has Feng Yuan / Yuan, matching the already proposed idiomatic repairs.

proposals.before: Hu and Yuan also secretly communicated with the capital.
proposals.after: Hu and Yang also secretly communicated with the capital.
proposals.reason: 馮鴦 is Feng Yang (鴦 yāng); the sealed literal still has Feng Yuan / Yuan, matching the already proposed idiomatic repairs.

proposals.before: Thereupon Jun's minister of education Murong Ping campaigned against Ping, leader of the army Moyu Gen campaigned against Yuan, minister of works Yang Wu campaigned against Chang, general Who Pacifies the Army Murong Zang attacked Li.
proposals.after: Thereupon Jun's minister of education Murong Ping campaigned against Ping, leader of the army Moyu Gen campaigned against Yang, minister of works Yang Wu campaigned against Chang, general Who Pacifies the Army Murong Zang attacked Li.
proposals.reason: 馮鴦 is Feng Yang (鴦 yāng); the sealed literal still has Yuan.

proposals.before: Afterward Ping led a host of three thousand and fled to Pingyang; Yuan fled to Yewang; Li fled to Xingyang; Chang fled to Shaoling; all submitted their hosts.
proposals.after: Afterward Ping led a host of three thousand and fled to Pingyang; Yang fled to Yewang; Li fled to Xingyang; Chang fled to Shaoling; all submitted their hosts.
proposals.reason: 馮鴦 is Feng Yang (鴦 yāng); the sealed literal still has Yuan.

proposals.before: Reaching this point, forty-nine years had passed, yet swift gallop was not diminished; Jun compared it to Bao's dappled team, ordered casting bronze to picture its likeness, personally composed inscription and praise, carved on its side, placed east of Ji's east-side gate.
proposals.after: By then it was forty-nine years old, yet its swift gallop was undiminished; Jun compared it to the Bao family’s dappled horse, ordered bronze cast to picture its likeness, personally composed an inscription and praise, carved beside it, and placed it east of Ji’s east-side gate.
proposals.reason: 至是，四十九歲矣 states the horse’s age (歲), not that forty-nine years had elapsed; 鮑氏驄 is the Bao family’s dappled horse, not Bao Shuya’s. Align literal with the already proposed idiomatic repair.

decisions.reason: 章武太守 and 郡兵 in the same sentence support commandery troops, not county militia.

decisions.reason: The personal name in text is 馮鴦, read Feng Yang.

鴦奔于野王 in the flight list matches 馮鴦.
眾潰 has no 石虎 or Shi Hu antecedent in s0294; the subject is Li Chan's force in the Li Chan narrative.
Same 索頭 witness as the idiomatic repair; literal must not retain Wuhuan.
Literal must spell Feng Yang from 馮鴦.
鴦 in the paired short form requires Yang in English.
